rv.q: Crazy Mama is, in the best sense, an actor’s theater and a writer’s theater at once: intimate, funny, harrowing, and finally radiant with the stubborn possibility that love can survive even what it cannot cure.
Thanks to both Purl and Williams, if your heart doesn’t break for Sharon, perhaps you should go see your cardiologist.
And it's one of the best (more-or-less) solo shows I've seen in ages.
Even with those slower passages, Crazy Mama is funny, compassionate, dramatic, and devastating.
A transformation begins in her eyes, travels into her face and then seems to spiral through her entire body, stretching almost like taffy until another human being stands before us.

cn.t: Critics praise Linda Purl's extraordinary multi-character performance in this moving memoir about growing up with a schizophrenic mother, noting how her virtuosity seamlessly serves the heartrending storytelling.
